summary: The source contract limits n to ten decimal digits, and one digit-square transition enters a fixed finite state space, so the legal domain cannot support honest runtime scaling.

workload_bound.unit: decimal digits in the initial value
workload_bound.source_constraint: The source-fidelity-verified constraint 1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1 limits every legal positive input to at most ten decimal digits.

replacement_checks.evidence: The first next_value call examines exactly d <= 10 digits and returns at most 81d <= 810. Every later state is therefore in the finite positive set 1..810 and has at most three digits. Before Floyd's pointers meet, the deterministic sequence can contain at most 810 distinct states, so the total number of constant-width digit transitions is bounded; this proves O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition, including happy termination at 1 and termination on a non-one cycle.
